Europe's east was reshuffled between 1217 and 1314. A Mongol khanate, a Lithuanian state and a restored Byzantium all appear. Here is what changed.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ In 1217 the biggest state in the east is Kyivan Rus'. By 1314 that space is dominated by the Golden Horde, the Mongol successor state that also held sway over the Russian principalities.

2/ The Mongols won at Legnica (9 April 1241) and Mohi (11 April 1241), then withdrew from central Europe. The traditional explanation links it to the death of Great Khan Ögedei, though historians debate it.
3/ The Golden Horde's power peaked under Özbeg Khan, who ruled from 1312 and adopted Islam.
4/ Lithuania barely registers in 1217. By 1314 it is a real state on the map. Its first king, Mindaugas, was crowned in 1251, and Vilnius became its capital in 1323.

5/ The Latin Empire, set up after the Fourth Crusade in 1204, ended in 1261. The Byzantines were back in Constantinople by 1314, though weaker. Read the full story in our newsletter: https://buttondown.com/forummapping
